record.original_question:
For ψ ∈ L2(R), define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for L2(R) if {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of L2(R).

Is the collection of all Riesz wavelets dense in L2(R) with respect to the L2 norm?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Is the collection of all Riesz wavelets dense in L2 (R)?

We say that ψ is a Riesz wavelet for H = H 2 (R) or L2 (R) if the wavelet system is a Riesz
basis of H. A Riesz basis in a Hilbert space H can be defined as an image of an orthonormal
basis under an invertible operator on H. Every Riesz basis has a dual Riesz basis. However,
the dual of Riesz wavelet system might not be a wavelet system. If it is, then we say that ψ
is a biorthogonal (Riesz) wavelet.

Definition 2.1. We say that ψ ∈ L2 (R) is an o.n. wavelet if the collection of translates and
                                           dyadic dilates
                                           (2.1)                         ψj,k (x) := 2j/2ψ(2j x − k),      j, k ∈ Z
                                           forms an o.n. basis of L2 (R).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a function $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and integers $j,k \in \mathbb{Z}$, define the dyadic translate–dilate
$$\psi_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2}\,\psi(2^j x - k), \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}.$$
A system $\{e_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \subset H$ in a separable Hilbert space $H$ is called a Riesz basis of $H$ if it is the image of an orthonormal basis of $H$ under a bounded invertible linear operator on $H$; equivalently, $\{e_n\}$ is complete in $H$ and there exist constants $0 < A \le B < \infty$ such that
$$A \sum_{n} |c_n|^2 \;\le\; \Big\| \sum_n c_n e_n \Big\|_H^2 \;\le\; B \sum_n |c_n|^2$$
for every finitely supported sequence $\{c_n\}$.

Call $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ a Riesz wavelet for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ if the wavelet system $\{\psi_{j,k} : j,k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

Let $\mathcal{R}$ denote the set of all Riesz wavelets for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Determine whether $\mathcal{R}$ is dense in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ with respect to the $L^2$ norm: that is, is it true that for every $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a Riesz wavelet $\psi \in \mathcal{R}$ with $\|f - \psi\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})} < \varepsilon$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. It is listed as an open problem in surveys of open problems in wavelet theory. Density of orthonormal wavelets in L^2(R) is known, and partial positive results are available (e.g., convex combinations of orthonormal wavelets often yield Riesz wavelets, and density holds for frame wavelets), but the general density of Riesz wavelets in L^2(R) does not appear to have been established.
